document.abstract: Suggestion has been made that a paper be prepared outlining the broad principles of photographic sound recording as practiced for motion pictures. If it is attempted to make such a paper deal with anything like adequacy with the many phases of this complex art, it would be nothing short of a book. However, it appears possible to present in reasonably brief space the essential principles of photographic sound recording systems and to supplement this with a bibliography which will at least give the reader a start in studying any special phases of the question. It is hoped that a paper of this type may serve a useful purpose in helping those who are suddenly confronted with the necessity of working in this field to gain a preliminary picture of what is involved in photographic sound recording, so that they can with less difficulty read the papers which discuss the various special problems.
